correctness.rationale: Exact harmonicity follows from the ambient Laplacian; geometric weights ensure normal convergence and a real-analytic kernel. A consecutive block of length at least the number of distinct nonzero complex nodes produces an invertible Vandermonde matrix. Cosine and sine block families recover projected aggregate coefficients and vertical weighted aggregates separately; the zero projection is handled by degree-zero and degree-one features. Every spherical fibre has at most two points with distinct heights, so all annihilating site coefficients vanish. The positive Gram sum and one-eigenvalue-per-degree spectrum then follow. Finite checker diagnostics are auxiliary, not substituted for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is an explicit real, rank-one-in-every-degree strictly positive definite two-sphere construction, with a new finite-fibre Vandermonde proof and explicit non-characteristic witness. Jäger (2020) and Guella–Jäger (2022/2023) state coefficient-support characterizations, while Buhmann–Jäger (2022) provides full-block sufficiency, none of which directly supplies the particular one-mode real construction. Targeted mathematical literature and indexed-result searches found no equivalent construction or stronger statement plainly covering it. Earlier constructions of nonisotropic strict-positive kernels are acknowledged and first priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An earlier sparse non-isotropic kernel construction outside the inspected papers might already realize rank one in every degree.

General-purpose finite-atomic uniqueness tools are known; the asserted novelty is the explicit real per-degree feature construction and its sharp spectral rank, not the abstract Vandermonde theorem or general SPD characterization.
No independent external priority or mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Determining whether strict interpolation on every finite subset of S² is compatible with the smallest nonzero spectral rank in each degree is a motivated structural sparsity problem. An explicit real-analytic real-valued kernel with exactly one positive spherical harmonic mode at every degree is an extremal spectral realization, not a narrow numerical table; the counterexample for probability-measure characteristicness identifies a useful boundary between finite-site interpolation and distributional identifiability. The construction is all-degree and all-site, while uniform stability and higher-dimensional extensions are explicitly not claimed.
